title: Finite Galois descent for sections of an etale sheaf
statement: Let $L$ be a field, let $E/L$ be a finite Galois extension (finite and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], normal, with $Q=\operatorname{Aut}_L(E)$ [def-pc-field-extension]), and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. The group $Q$ acts on $F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$ by pullback along the automorphisms of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ over $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Pullback along $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ identifies $F(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ bijectively with the subset of $Q$-invariant elements of $F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$.

source.place: Tag 04JM, Lemma lemma-global-sections-point, finite Galois descent argument

proof.text: Because $E/L$ is finite separable, $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. It is surjective because both spectra have one point, hence $\{\pi\}$ is a covering in the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Its self-intersection $W=\operatorname{Spec}E\times_{\operatorname{Spec}L}\operatorname{Spec}E$ is described by [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition]: (1) $E\otimes_LE\cong\prod_{q\in Q}E$, and (2) there is a bijection $\beta:F(W)\to\prod_{q\in Q}F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$ carrying restriction along the first projection $p_1$ to $s\mapsto(s)_q$ and restriction along the second projection $p_2$ to $s\mapsto((\operatorname{Spec}q)^*s)_q$.

source.place: Tag 03SF, finite etale objects under a finite Galois extension

proof.text: Apply the sheaf equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] to the one-member covering $\{\pi\}$ of step 1. It identifies $F(\operatorname{Spec}L)$, via $s\mapsto s|_\pi$, with the equalizer of $s\mapsto s|_{p_1}$ and $s\mapsto s|_{p_2}$ from $F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$ to $F(W)$. Since $\beta$ of [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition] (2) is a bijection, $s|_{p_1}=s|_{p_2}$ iff $\beta(s|_{p_1})=\beta(s|_{p_2})$, i.e. iff $(\operatorname{Spec}q)^*s=s$ for every $q\in Q$. The automorphisms of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ are exactly the $\operatorname{Spec}q$, $q\in Q$ (morphisms of affine schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ correspond to $L$-algebra maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), so the equalizer is exactly the set of $Q$-invariant sections.

source.place: Tag 04JM, Lemma lemma-global-sections-point, finite Galois descent argument

proof.text: The equalizer inclusion is the pullback map along $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}L$, so it is injective, and step 2 shows that every $Q$-invariant section is its pullback. Therefore pullback identifies $F(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ bijectively with the $Q$-invariant subset of $F(\operatorname{Spec}E)$.

source.place: Tag 04JM, Lemma lemma-global-sections-point, conclusion of the finite Galois descent argument
